facts: The proposed approach associates objects across multiple PTZ cameras.
The proposed approach can be used to perform camera handoff in wide-area surveillance scenarios.
Previous approaches relied on geometric information for establishing correspondences between static cameras.
Previous approaches relied on correlation-based information for establishing correspondences between static cameras.
Previous approaches are not extendable to wide-area settings with PTZ cameras.
In the proposed approach, the slave camera only passively follows the target.
The slave camera bootstraps itself from its own incoming imagery.
The proposed approach circumvents the problems faced by previous approaches.
The proposed approach avoids the need to perform any model transfer.
A novel Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) formulation for the problem is proposed.
The Multiple Instance Learning formulation is based on the logistic softmax function of covariance-based region features.
The Multiple Instance Learning formulation is within a MAP estimation framework.
The approach is demonstrated with multiple PTZ camera sequences in typical outdoor surveillance settings.
The approach is compared with state-of-the-art approaches.
entities: camera handoff in wide-area surveillance scenarios
logistic softmax function of covariance-based region features
